questions.q: What does SET STATISTICS PROFILE show?
options: A text-based result set listing every operator with estimated vs. actual row counts and cost
A graphical plan tree only
The T-SQL syntax tree
A list of every user connected to the database
questions.explain: It interleaves an extra result set of plain rows/columns describing each operator's estimates and actuals.

questions.q: What is the status of SET STATISTICS PROFILE today?
options: Deprecated — kept for backward compatibility, not recommended for new work
It's the newest, recommended way to view plans
It was removed entirely from SQL Server
It only works in Azure SQL, not on-premises
questions.explain: Microsoft has marked it deprecated in favor of the graphical plan and SET STATISTICS XML.

questions.q: What does SET STATISTICS XML return?
options: The actual execution plan as an XML value in the results grid, alongside the query's normal results
Only the estimated plan, never the actual one
A CSV export of the results
The query's raw T-SQL text
questions.explain: It returns the plan as XML data you can click to open graphically, or save and store.

questions.q: What is a .sqlplan file used for?
options: A saved snapshot of an execution plan you can reopen graphically later without re-running the query
A backup of an entire database
A script that automatically tunes indexes
A log of every query run that day
questions.explain: Double-clicking a .sqlplan file reopens the exact graphical plan tree that was captured, no re-execution needed.

questions.q: Why capture a plan as XML instead of just reading the Ctrl+M graphical plan in the moment?
options: The graphical plan disappears when the tab closes, but an XML/.sqlplan snapshot is durable and can be compared before vs. after a change
XML plans run faster than graphical ones
Graphical plans can't show Index Seeks
XML is required for the query to execute at all
questions.explain: Saving the plan as data lets you keep a permanent before/after record instead of relying on memory of a plan you already closed.
